orion.materials: Can you spare ten metal? A few roofs need patching, and I'd rather get people dry before somebody invents a form for it.
orion.housing-report: The new homes are finished. I've already handed over the keys. Didn't see much point making people wait for a ceremony.
orion.housing-plan: I've got plans for more homes. Nothing fancy, just decent places to live. Give me the go-ahead and we'll put the space to good use.
orion.power-report: The power grid's behaving itself. One generator needed a little encouragement, but we're calling that a successful repair rather than an argument with machinery.
orion.public-meeting: Two groups of settlers are arguing again. I'd like to sit them down and let everybody have their say before this turns ugly. You all right with that?
orion.trade-route: Some traders offered us a regular supply route. Their prices look fair, and I made sure the workers get a fair deal too. Shall I sign it?
orion.patrol-report: The patrol found a stranded traveller. We gave them food and somewhere warm to sleep. Quiet perimeter, one less person freezing outside. I'll call that a good day.
orion.garden-plan: We've got enough grey walls. How about a covered garden? Somewhere people can sit without feeling like they're waiting for orders. Can I get your approval?
orion.salvage-plan: There's abandoned machinery out near the survey site. Might be useful, might be scrap. Want me to send a crew to check it, or leave it where it is?
orion.settlement-report: People are starting to call this place home. That's a good feeling. Come visit when you can; you shouldn't only see the settlement when something's gone wrong.

khazglar.materials: Bring me ten metal, would you? These repairs need proper plates, not another hopeful layer of sealant.
khazglar.housing-report: Housing block's finished. Solid walls, sound joints, decent roofs. Built it to last longer than the people who commissioned it.
khazglar.housing-plan: We need more homes. I've drawn up the foundations already. Give the word and I'll put the crews to work.
khazglar.power-report: Generators are serviced. Replaced a worn coupling before it failed. That's maintenance: fixing trouble before it earns a name.
khazglar.public-meeting: The settlers have grievances. Best hear them now, before somebody settles an argument with a spanner. Shall I call a meeting?
khazglar.trade-route: A supplier's offering regular shipments. I checked their samples; the metal's good. Do you want me to agree to the route?
khazglar.patrol-report: Perimeter inspection's done. Found loose bolts on a watchtower. Tightened them. No enemies, unless you count whoever installed them.
khazglar.garden-plan: I'd like a covered garden. People mend better when they've somewhere pleasant to sit. Approve it, and I'll find the space.
khazglar.salvage-plan: Survey found an old machine outside the settlement. Could be useful beneath the rust. Permission to send a salvage crew?
khazglar.settlement-report: Come by the workshop sometime. You don't need a broken ship as an excuse. There's a spare chair, if you move the tools.

james.materials: I've got repairs waiting and not enough metal. Ten units would cover it. Can you help me keep this place standing?
james.housing-report: The new homes are ready. Checked every door myself. Nobody here should have to wonder whether their shelter will hold.
james.housing-plan: More families are arriving. We could expand the housing district before it gets crowded. Your decision; I'll carry it out.
james.power-report: Backup power's working. I tested it twice. I've had enough unpleasant surprises to last several lifetimes.
james.public-meeting: Some residents want to speak about how we're running things. I'd rather listen than give them a reason to fear us. Shall I arrange it?
james.trade-route: We've been offered a supply agreement. I checked who we'd be dealing with. Looks clean, but I want your approval first.
james.patrol-report: Patrols are back. Everyone accounted for, perimeter clear. I keep checking the names. Old habits, I suppose.
james.garden-plan: Someone asked for a covered garden. I almost dismissed it as a luxury. Maybe that's exactly why we should consider it. What do you think?
james.salvage-plan: There's abandoned equipment nearby. I'd send people to inspect it, but only with your permission. I'm done making those decisions behind your back.
james.settlement-report: You trusted me with this place. I haven't forgotten what that cost you. I'm trying to make sure the people here never regret it.

kizna.materials: Maintenance stock is low. Ten units of metal would clear the repair queue. Would you authorize the transfer?
kizna.housing-report: The housing block is complete. All rooms passed inspection. The residents have already begun moving the furniture into less efficient positions.
kizna.housing-plan: Population projections indicate a need for additional housing. Expansion plans are ready. Do you approve construction?
kizna.power-report: Primary and reserve power systems passed their tests. No faults detected. I have scheduled another inspection, in case they become overconfident.
kizna.public-meeting: Several residents have requested a public meeting. Their concerns merit attention. May I organize the discussion?
kizna.trade-route: A trader has proposed regular deliveries. Prices and reliability meet our requirements. Shall I accept the agreement?
kizna.patrol-report: Patrol report received. No threats detected, and all personnel returned safely. A satisfactory outcome on every relevant measure.
kizna.garden-plan: Residents have requested a covered garden. Recreational space appears to improve morale. Do you approve the allocation?
kizna.salvage-plan: Survey personnel located abandoned machinery. Condition unknown. Shall I dispatch a salvage crew or mark the site as undisturbed?
kizna.settlement-report: No urgent matters require your attention. You may visit for nonessential conversation. I am told those visits are often the most appreciated.

charon.materials: The repair crews need ten metal. I'd lend them a piece of myself, but most of my remaining parts are spoken for.
charon.housing-report: New housing is ready. The doors open, the heaters work, and nobody has complained yet. A promising start by station standards.
charon.housing-plan: I've prepared a housing expansion. Plenty of room, sensible access, no corridors ending in walls. Shall we build it?
charon.power-report: Power checks complete. The backup generator is older than its maintenance manual, but we understand each other.
charon.public-meeting: Residents want a meeting. I've repaired enough shared machinery to know that ignoring complaints rarely makes them quieter. May I arrange it?
charon.trade-route: A supplier offered us a regular route. I know what reliable deliveries are worth. Would you like me to accept?
charon.patrol-report: Perimeter is clear. One patrol unit reported a suspicious noise. Turned out to be its own knee joint. I can sympathize.
charon.garden-plan: How would you feel about a covered garden? I cannot enjoy the scent, but I could install excellent irrigation.
charon.salvage-plan: There's discarded machinery near the survey site. Discarded does not always mean useless. Shall I send someone to look?
charon.settlement-report: I used to spend my days waiting for somebody to need a repair. It is rather pleasant when people simply stop to say hello.

nyrexia.materials: Could you spare ten units of metal? There are homes in need of repair, and I would rather not leave their residents waiting.
nyrexia.housing-report: The new housing block is complete. A family invited me in to see their little kitchen. I think I smiled all afternoon.
nyrexia.housing-plan: I would like to extend the housing district. Everyone deserves a little privacy and a door of their own. May we proceed?
nyrexia.power-report: The engineers have checked our power systems. Everything is sound. I made sure their work was thanked properly.
nyrexia.public-meeting: Some residents feel their concerns have gone unheard. May I hold an open meeting? Listening is part of the position you've given me.
nyrexia.trade-route: A merchant has proposed regular supplies. The terms seem fair to both sides. Would you approve the agreement?
nyrexia.patrol-report: Our patrols returned safely. I spoke with them before they rested; there is nothing troubling to report.
nyrexia.garden-plan: Could we build a covered garden? Vishara always understood what a beautiful place could mean to people. I'd like to give them that here.
nyrexia.salvage-plan: The survey team found abandoned equipment. It may help the settlement, if it is safe. May I send a crew to inspect it?
nyrexia.settlement-report: I miss my sister, sometimes. But being trusted with the people here means a great deal to me. Thank you for giving me the chance.

custom-species.materials: Our repair workers need ten units of metal. Could you provide them? We are learning how to make these buildings endure.
custom-species.housing-report: The new homes are ready. Their residents are already changing them to suit their lives. I enjoy seeing what they choose.
custom-species.housing-plan: More people wish to settle here. I have prepared room for another housing district. Do you approve the expansion?
custom-species.power-report: The power systems are stable. I spent some time with the engineers today. There is still much in their work that fascinates me.
custom-species.public-meeting: Different customs have led to a few disagreements. I would like everyone to explain their concerns at a public meeting. May I arrange it?
custom-species.trade-route: Traders have offered a regular supply route. It may bring useful goods and new visitors. Shall we accept their proposal?
custom-species.patrol-report: The perimeter is quiet. Our patrols are learning the land well; they now notice changes I would have missed.
custom-species.garden-plan: May we set aside space for a covered garden? I would like the people here to share the living things they find beautiful.
custom-species.salvage-plan: A survey crew discovered abandoned machinery. We do not yet know its purpose. Shall I authorize an inspection or leave it untouched?
custom-species.settlement-report: I once wondered whether I would ever belong among people so different from me. Today, someone called this our home. I liked that.

gareth.materials: Got ten metal going spare? The roofs need fixing. Apparently being the Uxbridge Top Shotter doesn't make me a qualified roofer.
gareth.housing-report: New homes are done! I checked the stairs personally. Every single one. Some of them with my face.
gareth.housing-plan: I've got a plan for more houses. Proper homes, decent space. Can I get the go-ahead before somebody turns it into another car park?
gareth.power-report: Power's sorted. Didn't shoot the generator, before you ask. Turns out the engineers have a special tool called a screwdriver.
gareth.public-meeting: A few settlers want a meeting. I can keep it civil. Mostly. You happy for me to hear them out?
gareth.trade-route: Traders are offering regular deliveries. Good prices, too. Shall I sign it, or do you want me to negotiate with my very impressive personality?
gareth.patrol-report: Patrols found nothing dangerous. I did fall over a bollard, but that's between you, me, and about twelve witnesses.
gareth.garden-plan: Hear me out: a covered garden. Benches, flowers, somewhere nice to sit. Can I have approval for one good idea that doesn't involve pistols?
gareth.salvage-plan: We've found some abandoned machinery. Could be worth a fortune! Could also be a very expensive fridge. Want me to send a crew?
gareth.settlement-report: Uxbridge Top Shotter, governor, occasional public embarrassment. Busy life. Come visit sometime; I'll give you the tour and try to stay upright.

peter.materials: I need ten metal for repairs. Can you spare it? I'd rather fix the bloody roofs than listen to another complaint about loose panels.
peter.housing-report: The new homes are finished. People have moved in, and the walls are still standing. That's a decent day's work.
peter.housing-plan: We need more houses. I've got a plan that works. Give me approval and I'll get the damn thing started.
peter.power-report: Power's back to behaving itself. The engineers fixed the fault. I stood nearby looking threatening, which I'm claiming helped.
peter.public-meeting: A few residents have complaints. I'd rather let them speak than have the whole place muttering behind closed doors. Shall I call a meeting?
peter.trade-route: There's a supply deal on the table. Fair terms, no obvious bullshit. Do you want me to accept it?
peter.patrol-report: Patrols are back. Nothing tried to break in. Almost disappointing, but I suppose that's what we're aiming for.
peter.garden-plan: The residents want a covered garden. Before you laugh, I think they're right. Can I tell them you've approved it?
peter.salvage-plan: There's abandoned machinery out there. Might be useful, might be fucked. Shall I send a crew to find out?
peter.settlement-report: Place is running. People are safe. For once, nobody needs me to drag some idiot across the floor. I could get used to this.

josiah.materials: I require ten units of metal for repairs. Even a man returned from the grave cannot mend a roof with indignation alone.
josiah.housing-report: The new homes are complete. Their residents sleep safely tonight. That is an achievement worth more than any speech I could give.
josiah.housing-plan: I propose another housing district. Let our people see that we intend to build something lasting. Will you approve the plans?
josiah.power-report: The power systems have passed inspection. I commended the engineers. Quiet competence deserves recognition, even from me.
josiah.public-meeting: Our residents wish to be heard. I would convene a public meeting and give them that opportunity. Do I have your permission?
josiah.trade-route: A merchant has offered regular supplies on acceptable terms. I see merit in the arrangement. Shall I give our agreement?
josiah.patrol-report: Patrols report a clear perimeter. Good. I would prefer our enemies to remain a matter for the patrol reports rather than the repair crews.
josiah.garden-plan: I request approval for a covered garden. A settlement should give people something to enjoy as well as somewhere to endure.
josiah.salvage-plan: The survey team discovered abandoned machinery. I recommend an inspection before we declare it worthless. May I dispatch a salvage crew?
josiah.settlement-report: I came back expecting more battles. I did not expect to care whether a street was lit or a family had a home. Life is proving interesting.

croxian.materials: The repair teams need ten units of metal. I could order them to make do, but I have seen what happens when commanders value appearances over working equipment. Can you supply it?
croxian.housing-report: The housing block is finished. No barracks, no compulsory inspections of private rooms. Actual homes. A few residents seemed surprised when I handed them their keys.
croxian.housing-plan: I have a proposal for another housing district. The engineers have checked the foundations and evacuation routes. Will you authorise construction?
croxian.power-report: The reserve generators passed their tests. I stayed for the entire inspection. Being responsible for a city means learning what keeps it alive when nobody is firing a weapon.
croxian.public-meeting: Some residents disagree with the new work schedules. My first instinct was to issue an order. Instead, I would like to hear their objections at a public meeting. Do you approve?
croxian.trade-route: A trading company has offered regular deliveries. I checked its ownership and the terms of the contract. No hidden military obligations. Shall I accept their offer?
croxian.patrol-report: The patrols are back and everyone is accounted for. I have told them to report damaged streetlights as well as suspicious activity. People should feel safe walking home.
croxian.garden-plan: A group of children asked whether we could build a covered garden. I had no sensible reason to refuse them. Can I approve the space and materials?
croxian.salvage-plan: Surveyors found abandoned equipment outside the settlement. I would prefer a small inspection team to a dramatic expedition with unnecessary casualties. May I send them?
croxian.settlement-report: Someone thanked me in the market today. No rank, no salute. Just a thank-you. I am still getting used to earning respect without demanding it.

malia.materials: The repair schedule is ready, but we are ten units of metal short. Approve the transfer and I can clear the urgent work before it becomes an emergency.
malia.housing-report: The housing block is complete. Every room has heat, clean water and a working fire alarm. I inspected the shared facilities with the residents before signing it off.
malia.housing-plan: Population growth is outpacing our spare accommodation. I recommend another housing district, with services installed before anyone moves in. Do I have your approval?
malia.power-report: The power grid and reserve generators passed inspection. I have staggered future maintenance so we will not lose both systems on the same day.
malia.public-meeting: Residents have raised concerns about the distribution of work. I want an open meeting, with the decisions recorded and available to everyone. Will you authorise it?
malia.trade-route: The proposed trade route meets our supply requirements. I negotiated delivery penalties and an emergency reserve. Shall I sign the agreement?
malia.patrol-report: Perimeter patrols completed their rounds without incident. I have adjusted the shifts so nobody is finishing a night watch and starting a construction shift immediately after it.
malia.garden-plan: The settlement needs somewhere to rest as well as somewhere to work. A covered garden is a practical investment in morale. May I allocate the site?
malia.salvage-plan: Abandoned machinery has been located near the survey boundary. I have prepared a recovery plan with a safety inspection before transport. Shall the salvage crew proceed?
malia.settlement-report: There is nothing urgent to report. Deliveries arrived, wages were recorded, and the clinic opened on time. Good administration rarely makes an exciting story. I consider that a success.

williams.materials: Could you spare ten units of metal for the repair crews? I promised the residents we would put their homes right. I would like to be someone who keeps that sort of promise.
williams.housing-report: The new homes are finished. One family invited me in for tea, even though they had barely unpacked. I had forgotten how much an ordinary afternoon could mean.
williams.housing-plan: I have helped draw up another housing district. The architects did the difficult part, of course. Would you approve it? There are families who could really use the room.
williams.power-report: The power checks are complete. I asked the engineers to walk me through the backup systems. I am still learning, but I can finally be useful without pretending to know everything.
williams.public-meeting: Some residents want to talk about how the settlement is run. My grandfather used to say you cannot advise people you never listen to. May I arrange a public meeting?
williams.trade-route: A merchant has proposed regular deliveries. I went through the terms with our quartermaster, twice. They seem fair. Would you like me to agree to the route?
williams.patrol-report: The patrols returned safely. I met them at the gate and learned a few more names. It helps to remember that a settlement is people, not a number on a report.
williams.garden-plan: There is a sheltered site that would make a lovely covered garden. Somewhere quiet, where people could sit without needing a reason. Could we build it?
williams.salvage-plan: The survey team found some abandoned equipment. They think a little of it can be repaired. Shall I send a salvage crew? I would like to give it a chance before we write it off.
williams.settlement-report: I spent so long thinking I would be the last thing my family ever amounted to. Today I helped someone open a shop. Perhaps that is enough for one day. Thank you for giving me somewhere to begin.

tyrotaronus.materials: Our repair stores require ten units of metal. The work is necessary, and I have recorded how each unit will be used. Will you authorise the transfer?
tyrotaronus.housing-report: The housing block is complete. Homes were allocated by need, without preference for rank, species or former allegiance. The register is available if you wish to inspect it.
tyrotaronus.housing-plan: I propose an additional housing district. Our present capacity is adequate, but waiting for overcrowding would leave us with fewer reasonable choices. Do you approve the expansion?
tyrotaronus.power-report: Primary and reserve power systems passed their inspections. Both teams followed the same procedure. A familiar machine deserves the same scrutiny as an unfamiliar one.
tyrotaronus.public-meeting: Two groups of residents have brought conflicting claims to my office. I would hear both in a public meeting, under the same rules. May I proceed?
tyrotaronus.trade-route: The proposed supply agreement imposes obligations on both parties. I find the terms balanced and enforceable. Shall I accept it on the settlement's behalf?
tyrotaronus.patrol-report: Patrols have completed their rounds. A visitor's documents were delayed, so I arranged shelter while the matter was resolved. Following a procedure does not require needless suffering.
tyrotaronus.garden-plan: The residents have requested a covered garden. Rest has a place in a functioning settlement, just as work does. May I reserve the land for it?
tyrotaronus.salvage-plan: Our survey team located abandoned machinery. Before recovery, they will check for an owner and any hazard to the settlement. Do you authorise the salvage investigation?
tyrotaronus.settlement-report: No urgent decision is required today. People kept their agreements, disputes were heard, and the settlement continued its work. Balance is often quieter than those who speak in its name.
